question: Will U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs record a single-day net inflow exceeding $500 million on any trading day between August 31 and September 7, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Window is 5 trading days (Aug 31, Sep 1-4); Labor Day Sep 7 is excluded by the criteria. Farside totals already published: Aug 31 +216.7, Sep 1 -236.5, Sep 2 +101.15 — all well short. So YES requires Sep 3 or Sep 4 alone to clear +500. Reference class: 2026 YTD days above +$500m are roughly 5-6 out of ~168 sessions (~3-4%/day) — Jan 6 +697.2, a mid-Jan +753/+843.6 pair, at least one early-May day, and Aug 19 +517.2 / Aug 20 +606.3. Even in August, the best flow month of 2026 (+$3.52bn, 16 of 21 positive sessions, a 9-day streak), only 2 of 21 days cleared the bar, and the Aug 24-31 tail ran +314.3, +232.2, +242.3, ~-1, +216.7 — the streak's biggest days were nowhere near +500. Upward pull: BTC rallied ~3% to ~$81.3k on Sep 3 on Waller/Fed-pause comments after dipping below $78k, with reported renewed institutional bid and Strategy resuming purchases; large inflow days cluster on strong rally days. Downward pull: this week's flow response to price has been weak (Sep 2 was an up day for BTC yet only +101m), IBIT's recent best single-day was ~+278m and would need ~+400m to carry a 500-total, and only two candidate days remain. Two days at a rally-conditioned ~4-5%/day, with positive correlation between them, gives ~8%; a small extra haircut for the chance Sep 4's figure is not published before the Sep 5 00:00Z resolution stamp keeps it there.

disagreements.claim: Whether a human market prices this event (Run 2 found a Polymarket daily flow contract; Runs 1 and 3 found none)
disagreements.verdict: Settled and reconciled: Run 2's contract resolves off the same Farside Total but is positive-vs-negative with no $500m threshold and had $0 volume. Non-matching contract, zero liquidity — evidence of nothing. No anchor exists from any venue.

disagreements.claim: Whether the Sep 4 row will be published before the 2026-09-05T00:00Z resolution stamp
disagreements.verdict: Unsettled — no run found a stated Farside posting-time guarantee, and empirically the Sep 3 row was still absent at 23:31 UK. The criteria text includes Sep 4 regardless, so I apply only a small haircut to Sep 4's effective exposure rather than excluding it.

disagreements.claim: Governing reference class for the two remaining days: 2026 YTD (~3-4%/day) vs post-Aug-17 regime (2/13 = ~15%)
disagreements.verdict: Neither raw. The 15% is conditioned on a nine-session inflow streak that ended before this window, so it overstates; the 3-4% unconditional understates a strong rally session, which is the only condition under which +500 prints have ever occurred. I take the conditional reading: ~10% for Sep 3, ~5% for Sep 4.

disagreements.claim: How much weight the Sep 3 rally deserves given weak price-to-flow transmission this week
disagreements.verdict: No evidence breaks this tie — the Sep 3 flow is unpublished. I bet on the dampened reading: Sep 2 was an up price day for only +101m, and the closest in-regime rally analogue (Aug 25 to ~$81.1k) produced +314, so a rally is necessary but historically not sufficient for +500 in this regime.

calls.reference_class: US spot Bitcoin ETF regular trading sessions with Farside aggregate Total above +$500m, 2026 YTD (~3-4% of ~168 sessions) and within the Aug-17-onward regime (2 of 13), conditioned on same-day BTC rally sessions in that regime
